an4.128:1.1: “Monks, with the appearance of the Tathāgata—the Worthy One, the Rightly Self-awakened One—four amazing & astounding things appear.
an4.128:1.3: “People find pleasure in longing, delight in longing, rejoice in longing.
an4.128:1.4: But when the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma of non-longing, they want to listen; they lend ear and set their minds on understanding it.
an4.128:1.5: This is the first amazing & astounding thing that appears with the appearance of the Tathāgata—the Worthy One, the Rightly Self-awakened One.
an4.128:2.1: “People find pleasure in conceit, delight in conceit, rejoice in conceit.
an4.128:2.2: But when the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma for the subduing of conceit, they want to listen; they lend ear and set their minds on understanding it.
an4.128:2.3: This is the second amazing & astounding thing that appears with the appearance of the Tathāgata—the Worthy One, the Rightly Self-awakened One.
an4.128:3.1: “People find pleasure in commotion, delight in commotion, rejoice in commotion.
an4.128:3.2: But when the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma for stilling, they want to listen; they lend ear and set their minds on understanding it.
an4.128:3.3: This is the third amazing & astounding thing that appears with the appearance of the Tathāgata—the Worthy One, the Rightly Self-awakened One.
an4.128:4.1: “People are immersed in ignorance, blinded,1 entirely enveloped.
an4.128:4.2: But when the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma for the subduing of ignorance, they want to listen; they lend ear and set their minds on understanding it.
an4.128:4.3: This is the fourth amazing & astounding thing that appears with the appearance of the Tathāgata—the Worthy One, the Rightly Self-awakened One.
an4.128:4.4: “Monks, with the appearance of the Tathāgata—the Worthy One, the Rightly Self-awakened One—these four amazing & astounding things appear.”
